messages.content:
Poem: Медный всадник, 01.json

RUSSIAN LINES
R0: Предисловие
R1: Происшествие, описанное в сей повести, основано на истине. Подробности наводнения заимствованы из тогдашних журналов. Любопытные могут справиться с известием, составленным В. Н. Берхом.
R2: Вступление
R3: На берегу пустынных волн
R4: Стоял он, дум великих полн,
R5: И вдаль глядел. Пред ним широ́ко
R6: Река неслася; бедный чёлн
R7: По ней стремился одиноко.
R8: По мшистым, топким берегам
R9: Чернели избы здесь и там,
R10: Приют убогого чухонца;
R11: И лес, неведомый лучам
R12: В тумане спрятанного солнца,
R13: Кругом шумел.
R14: И думал он:
R15: Отсель грозить мы будем шведу,
R16: Здесь будет город заложён
R17: На зло надменному соседу.
R18: Природой здесь нам суждено
R19: В Европу прорубить окно,
R20: Ногою твёрдой стать при море.
R21: Сюда по новым им волнам
R22: Все флаги в гости будут к нам,
R23: И запируем на просторе.
R24: Прошло сто лет, и юный град,
R25: Полнощных стран краса и диво,
R26: Из тьмы лесов, из топи блат
R27: Вознёсся пышно, горделиво;
R28: Где прежде финский рыболов,
R29: Печальный пасынок природы,

ENGLISH LINES
E0: On the waste shore of raving waves
E1: He stood, with high and dread thoughts filled,
E2: And gazed afar. Before him rolled
E3: The river wide, a fragile bark
E4: Its tortuous path slow making.
E5: Upon the moss-grown banks and swamps
E6: Stood far asunder smoky huts,
E7: The homes of Finnish fishers poor;
E8: Whilst all around, a forest wild,
E9: Unpierced by misty-circled sun,
E10: Murmured loud.
E11: Gazing far, he thought:
E12: From hence we can the Swede best threat;
E13: Here must I found a city strong,
E14: That shall our haughty foe bring ill;
E15: It is by nature's law decreed,
E16: That here we break a window through,
E17: And boldly into Europe look,
E18: And on the sea with sure foot stand;
E19: By water path as yet unknown,
E20: Shall ships from distant ports arrive,
E21: And far ard wide our reign extend.
E22: A hundred years have passed, and now,
E23: In place of forests dark and swamps,
E24: A city new, in pomp unmatched,
E25: Of Northern lands the pride and gem.
E26: Where Finnish fisher once at eve,
E27: Harsh nature's poor abandoned child,
E28: From low-sunk boat was wont his net
E29: With patient toil to cast, and drag
E30: The stream, now stretch long lines of quays,
E31: Of richest granite formed, and rows
E32: Of buildings huge and lordly domes
E33: The river front; whilst laden ships
E34: From distant quarters of the world
E35: Our hungry wharfs fresh spoils supply;
E36: And needful bridge its span extends,
E37: To join the stream's opposing shores;
E38: And islets gay, in verdure clad,
E39: Beneath the shade of gardens laugh.
E40: Before the youthful city's charms
E41: Her head proud Moscow jealous bends,

E38: And islets gay, in verdure clad,

E40: Before the youthful city's charms
E41: Her head proud Moscow jealous bends,
E42: As when the new Tsaritza young
E43: The widowed Empress lowly greets.
E44: I love thee, work of Peter's hand!
E45: I love thy stern, symmetric form;

Poem: Медный всадник, 02.json

RUSSIAN LINES
R0: Над омрачённым Петроградом
R1: Дышал ноябрь осенним хладом.
R2: Плеская шумною волной
R3: В края своей ограды стройной,
R4: Нева металась, как больной
R5: В своей постеле беспокойной.
R6: Уж было поздно и темно;
R7: Сердито бился дождь в окно,
R8: И ветер дул, печально воя.
R9: В то время из гостей домой
R10: Пришёл Евгений молодой…
R11: Мы будем нашего героя
R12: Звать этим именем. Оно
R13: Звучит приятно; с ним давно
R14: Моё перо к тому же дружно.
R15: Прозванья нам его не нужно,
R16: Хотя в минувши времена
R17: Оно, быть может, и блистало
R18: И под пером Карамзина
R19: В родных преданьях прозвучало;
R20: Но ныне светом и молвой
R21: Оно забыто. Наш герой
R22: Живёт в Коломне; где-то служит,
R23: Дичится знатных и не тужит
R24: Ни о почиющей родне,
R25: Ни о забытой старине.
R26: Итак, домой пришед, Евгений
R27: Стряхнул шинель, разделся, лёг.
R28: Но долго он заснуть не мог
R29: В волненье разных размышлений.

E0: Their bondage ancient and their feud;
E1: Nor let them with their idle hate
E2: Disturb great Peter's deathless sleep!
E3: It was a day of fear and dread,
E4: In book of memory still writ.
E5: And now, for you, my friends, the tale
E6: Of that day's woe I will begin;
E7: And mournful will my story be.
E8: O'er Peter's cloud-wrapt city hung
E9: November's autumn cold and mist.
E10: With noisy splash of angry wave
E11: The Neva chafed her granite fence,
E12: As one, confined to bed with pain,
E13: Will peevish toss from side to side.
E14: The hour was late, and it was dark,
E15: The rain beat hard on window-pane,
E16: The wind with mournful howl roared loud,
E17: When young Evjenie bade his friends
E18: Adieu, and homeward turned his steps.
E19: Evjenie is our hero's name,
E20: A name that lightly falls in verse,
E21: And one my pen is used to write.
E22: No interest his surname has,
E23: Though in the olden times gone by,
E24: May be, it was in high repute;
E25: We meet with it in Karamsin,
E26: Like other once familiar names;
E27: But now 'tis lost and all unknown.
E28: In district called Kolumna lived
E29: Our hero, who in office served.
E30: His chiefs he feared, but patient bore
E31: Death of relations dear and near,
E32: Or world's neglect of service past.
E33: Evjenie reached his home, uphung
E34: His cloak, undressed, and went to bed.
E35: But long it was before he slept;
E36: A host of cares possessed his brain.
E37: He thought... of what? That he was poor
E38: And hard must toil, if he would bare
E39: Existence get, in freedom live,
E40: Or have his neighbour's good repute.
E41: Wished that God had but endowed him
E42: With greater wit, or better, wealth;
E43: For in our world are those who have

R26: Мазепа.

R29: Ты подозреньем сердце губишь:

E0: Forgets with her the plaguing toil,
E1: The noise and cares of outer world;
E2: Reveals to her, the timid maid,
E3: His hopes and fears, his wily schemes.
E4: But, though she ne'er regrets the past,
E5: At times, a thick and labouring cloud
E6: Creeps o'er and darkens all her soul.
E7: Before her rise the griefful forms
E8: Of father stern and mother pale;
E9: With dimming eyes she sees them there,
E10: Abandoned in their childless age,
E11: And thinks to hear their soft reproach.

E13: The common talk of the Ukraine!

E15: The secret of revenge and crime.

E17: Is tossed with fear of failure's shame.
E18: Marie, with wistful eyes of love,
E19: In silence watches her old man,
E20: Approaching softly, clasps his knee,
E21: And sweet words whispers in his ear.
E22: In vain: no more her love has strength
E23: To chase away his musings dark.
E24: Cold he lowers his absent glance
E25: Before the kneeling maid, nor deigns
E26: Reply to her reproaching look.

E28: Half choked, she rises from her knees.
E29: nListen, Hetman", she cries,,,for thee
E30: I have forgotten home and all.
E31: And when my soul chose thee her lord,
E32: I had but one desire... thy love:
E33: For that I sacrificed my all!
E34: Nor do I now regret the past.

E36: The night I gave myself to thee,
E37: To love me ever thou didst swear:
E38: Tell me, then, why thy love has ceased.
E39: Hearken, Marie, thou art unjust.
E40: Shake off these vain and childish fears!
E41: Let not doubt sow poison in thy heart,
E42: Or blinded passion idly stir
E43: And vex thy young and ardent soul.

E5: Whilst, bent on him, each look observant,
E6: Saw grief's deep trace and passion fervent
E7: Upon his gloomy brow revealed.
E8: But the proud Khan his dark eye raising,
E9: And on the courtiers fiercely gazing,
E10: Gave signal to them to begone!
E11: The chief, unwitnessed and alone,
E12: Now yields him to his bosom's smart,
E13: Deeper upon his brow severe
E14: Is traced the anguish of his heart;
E15: As full fraught clouds on mirrors clear
E16: Reflected terrible appear!

E36: Treason could never enter there.

E40: Which erst perfumed Arabia's field. To them the days in sameness dreary,

E42: In solitude, of life grown weary,
E43: Well pleased they see their charms decay.
E44: Each day, alas! the past resembling,
E45: Time loiters through their halls and bowers;

E543: The bard shall wind thy rocky ways
E544: Filled with fond sympathies, shall view
E545: Tauride's bright skies and waves of blue
E546: With greedy and enraptured gaze.
E547: Enchanting region! full of life
E548: Thy hills, thy woods, thy leaping streams,
E549: Ambered and rubied vines, all rife
E550: With pleasure, spot of fairy dreams!
E551: Valleys of verdure, fruits, and flowers,
E552: Cool waterfalls and fragrant bowers!
E553: All serve the traveller's heart to fill
E554: With joy as he in hour of morn
E555: By his accustomed steed is borne
E556: In safety o'er dell, rock, and hill,
E557: Whilst the rich herbage, bent with dews,
E558: Sparkles and rustles on the ground,
E559: As he his venturous path pursues
E560: Where AYOUDAHGA'S crags surround!
E561: [1] A Turkish pipe.
